questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The main reasons for choosing my study destination were the chance to experience a new culture, meet new people, and benefit from the academic opportunities.

Culturally, it was interesting to live in a different place and see how things are done there. Experiencing local traditions, food, and daily life made the experience more engaging.

Meeting new people was also important. Studying somewhere new meant getting to know students from different backgrounds, which made both the social and academic environment more dynamic.

Academically, the quality of education and available courses played a big role. The program offered relevant subjects and good learning opportunities, making it a solid choice.

Overall, it was a mix of personal and academic benefits that made the destination appealing.

questions.answer: It consists of smaller courses. around 5-6 ECTS. Both BA and MA students can take the same classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the style of teaching were very different. They take attendance and you need to participate in class since that is 20% of your grade. Further, you do not receive any books, so it is important to attend the classes in order to be able to pass the exam. There was also a lot of presentations which formed a part of your grade.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was okay. You primarily have classes with exchange students, and therefore spend most time with them. This of course meant many different cultures, but I found it very interesting to see how people are doing around the world.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One cultural difference that was particularly challenging was adjusting to different social norms and communication styles. For example, people might have a different approach to personal space, directness in conversation, or daily routines. Additionally, understanding local customs, such as dining habits or expectations in social settings, took some time. While these differences weren’t major obstacles, they required some adaptation to feel completely comfortable.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the social atmosphere and the emphasis on enjoying life. People seemed to prioritize spending time together, whether through long meals, gatherings, or casual conversations. The local food and dining culture were also highlights, offering a great way to connect with others. Additionally, the balance between work and leisure was something I found refreshing, as it encouraged a more relaxed and enjoyable daily life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find housing in good time, apply for additional grants, find housing in the center, instead og close to school.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students might find it useful to familiarize themselves with basic local customs and daily routines before arriving. Understanding how public transport works, typical meal times, can make the transition smoother. It’s also helpful to connect with current or former exchange students for practical tips and insights. Lastly, making an effort to engage with both local and international students can enhance the experience socially and academically.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting new
people.The
most rewarding part of the exchange experience was the opportunity to step out of my comfort zone and adapt to a new environment. Meeting people from different backgrounds, experiencing a new culture firsthand, and gaining a fresh perspective on academics made the experience both personally and professionally enriching. The connections made and the skills developed—such as independence, adaptability, and cross-cultural communication—were especially valuable.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during the exchange was adjusting to the differences in academic expectations and workload. The pace and structure of courses were sometimes different from what I was used to, requiring me to adapt quickly. Additionally, balancing academics with the social aspects of the exchange was sometimes tricky, as I wanted to make the most of both my studies and the cultural experiences.
